Title: Mismatch Negativity to Acoustical Illusion of Beat: How and Where the Brain Processes Binaural Beats
Summary: This study investigates mismatch negativity responses to binaural beats using magnetoencephalography (MEG). It highlights that binaural beats elicit neural activity primarily in the auditory cortex and involve early auditory processing. The findings support binaural beats as perceptible phenomena and outline their neural correlates.

Title: Representation of Dynamic Interaural Phase Difference in Auditory Cortex of Awake Rhesus Macaques
Authors: Brian H. Scott, Brian J. Malone, Michael N. Semple
Summary: Explores neural encoding of dynamic interaural phase differences in the auditory cortex of awake rhesus macaques. The study uses electrophysiological recordings to show how cortical neurons process spatial auditory information, relevant to understanding binaural sound localization.

Title: Binaural Beats at 0.25 Hz Shorten the Latency to Slow-Wave Sleep in Healthy Young Adults
Summary: This study evaluates the effects of 0.25 Hz binaural beats on sleep onset and quality. Findings demonstrate reduced sleep latency and enhanced slow-wave sleep using polysomnography. The results highlight binaural beats as a non-invasive approach to improving sleep quality.

Title: Gamma-Frequency Binaural Beats Enhance Cognitive Performance
Authors: L. Colzato, W. Barone, M. Sellaro, L. Hommel
Summary: Examines the impact of gamma-frequency binaural beats on attentional performance. Using global-local visual tasks, the study finds that binaural beats enhance top-down cognitive control, suggesting their potential to improve attention in real-world applications.

Title: Theta-Frequency Binaural Beats Reduce Pain and Analgesic Use in Chronic Pain Patients
Summary: Investigates theta-frequency binaural beats' effects on chronic pain. Results indicate significant reductions in pain intensity and reliance on analgesics, suggesting potential for binaural beats in non-invasive pain management strategies.

Title: Binaural Beat Technology in Humans: Effects on Neuropsychological and Physiological Outcomes
Authors: H. Wahbeh, C. Calabrese, H. Zwickey
Summary: This pilot study assesses the neuropsychological and physiological effects of binaural beats in healthy adults. Findings suggest reductions in anxiety and improvements in quality of life, warranting further research into their therapeutic potential.

Title: Auditory Evoked Responses to Binaural Beat Illusion: Stimulus Parameters and Electrophysiological Analysis
Summary: Examines the electrophysiological responses to binaural beats using auditory evoked potentials (AEPs). The study identifies neural responses to various stimulus parameters, contributing to understanding the auditory mechanisms underlying binaural beats.

Title: Neurophysiological Effects of Binaural Beats on Cognitive and Emotional States
Summary: Analyzes EEG responses to binaural beats at delta and theta frequencies. The study demonstrates mood improvements and reduced anxiety, linking binaural beats to potential cognitive and emotional benefits.
